investigations.question: In the core Sequence Paxos, if a follower's Accepted reply (or the leader's AcceptDecide) is lost, does any timer-driven or self-initiated mechanism restore the leader's knowledge of that acceptance, or does a quorum-accepted entry stay undecided until an unrelated new proposal arrives?
investigations.hypothesis: There is no repair for this direction: resend_messages_leader in Phase::Accept only resends a pending StopSign/its decide and re-Prepares peers that are not promised, and resend_messages_follower in Phase::Accept is an empty arm, so a lost Accepted is never retried by either side; the leader's decision only re-evaluates on a later handle_accepted, i.e. only when some follower accepts something new, which requires an unrelated proposal.
investigations.discriminator: A deterministic in-process simulation (real OmniPaxos instances with a memory storage, manual message delivery and logical ticks): elect a leader, propose one entry, let the follower accept it, drop only that follower's Accepted, then keep ticking and delivering for a fair window with no new proposals, and compare the leader's decided_idx against a control run in which the same message is delivered. If the entry stays undecided in the drop case while both the leader's own acceptance and the follower's accepted_idx show a quorum, the loss is repaired by nothing in that interval; if the entry becomes decided without the message or without a new proposal, the hypothesis is refuted.

interpretations.rationale: Current account. Source-settled mechanism: the actor publishes every observed transition with `event_tx.send(..).await` inside `detect_and_emit_events` (actor.rs:169-199), awaited from the tick arm of the single `run` select loop (actor.rs:665-711), on the channel spawn_actor builds as `async_channel::bounded(RuntimeConfig::event_capacity)` (handle.rs:295-323; knob handle.rs:34-35, default 1024 handle.rs:74). The handle owns a receiver from construction, so an application that never consumes the event stream still leaves it unread, and `subscribe_events` only hands out clones of that same channel (handle.rs:254-259). A `send` that cannot fit parks the actor task, which then cannot run `op.tick()` (election heartbeats, resends, batch flushes), cannot handle incoming messages, and cannot answer any Command - including the `append_notify` Timeout that `drain_notifiers` would have produced on that same tick path (actor.rs:201-222; endpoint documented at handle.rs:114-137). The crate's sibling egress paths avoid exactly this with `try_send` (drain_outgoing_buf; push_to_sub/push_to_all_subs) and its own regression test states the invariant for the outgoing channel. Recorded execution 011decb17a314e839b860436ad3dc164 (experiment 9a11299aa4344bb5b84565cbe33701ad-experiment, exit 0) ran the two-case harness against the clean copy and its test_selection reports both cases passed: `unconsumed_event_stream_stops_actor_loop` and `drained_event_stream_keeps_actor_loop_running` (nothing filtered out). Case 1 (event_capacity 64, paced 4ms proposals, no consumer) required and observed: all three event channels full (`len == capacity`, receiver not closed), at least one node whose actor never answered a `decided_idx` command across ten 200ms samples and still answered nothing 500ms later, and that node's `append_notify_with_timeout(.., 300ms)` unresolved after 4s although its `append_notify_timeout` is 1500ms. Case 2 (identical cluster, capacity and activity, with a task draining each event stream) required and observed the opposite: every node kept answering commands and a follower `append_notify` resolved `Ok(idx >= 1)`. Because the only difference between the cases is whether the event stream is consumed, the parking and the withheld endpoints are attributed to the unconsumed bounded event channel, not to the transport, the configuration or the harness. interpretations.rationale: Source-only current account of the new question, no execution yet. A follower replies to each AcceptDecide/AcceptStopSign with an Accepted that carries only the receipt's ballot and the follower's accepted_idx (follower.rs:160-175), and the leader turns those receipts into a decision when `is_chosen` sees a quorum of advertised accepted indexes (leader.rs:316-345). Both roles have a periodic callback - SequencePaxos::resend_message_timeout dispatches to resend_messages_leader/resend_messages_follower every resend_message_tick_timeout logical ticks (mod.rs:229-246) - but in the accept phase the leader's version only resends a pending StopSign (or its decide) and re-Prepares peers that are not promised (leader.rs:371-403), and the follower's version is the empty `Phase::Accept => ()` arm (follower.rs:240-269); the follower's other periodic path, flush_batch_follower, replies only when the batch flush itself advanced the accepted index (follower.rs:284-290). So the direction follower->leader has no timer-driven retry, and the leader has no way to ask a follower for its accepted index; the only later trigger is a new AcceptDecide arriving for new entries, which makes the follower advertise a (possibly larger) accepted_idx. Whether that leaves a genuinely quorum-accepted entry undecided for an unbounded interval with no enabled repair under normal (no further proposal) conditions is exactly what the registered discriminator is to decide; no defect is claimed before it runs.
limitations: The claim depends on the environment being permitted to lose a single message while the transport keeps the rest in order; the probe must drop only the Accepted reply and keep delivering everything else.

A retry of the client's own proposal (in the runtime layer) can repair the earlier entry as a side effect, so any later assertion must be scoped to 'no further proposal is made', which the core API does not itself require of a caller.

investigations.question: Can a full, undrained RuntimeConfig event channel (a subscribed but unread subscribe_events() receiver) stop the single actor task, and with it the node's whole consensus participation - ticks, message handling and every Command reply?

event_capacity 64 so the bound is reached inside a bounded window; the source-settled mechanism (send awaits when the channel holds event_capacity events) is capacity-independent
the handle's event receiver exists from construction, so an application that never subscribes still leaves it unread
excluded: schedule independence or any rate bound

basis.prefix: Three real OmniPaxos instances (pid 1,2,3) built with OmniPaxosConfig::build over omnipaxos_storage::memory_storage::MemoryStorage, each driven by a real omnipaxos_runtime actor from spawn_actor with a harness-local tokio-backed AsyncRuntime impl; one in-process transport task per node forwards each message from that node's outgoing_messages() to msg.get_receiver()'s handle_incoming. RuntimeConfig: tick_period 2ms, egress_period 1ms, event_capacity 64, append_notify_timeout 1500ms; ServerConfig: election_tick_timeout 3, resend_message_tick_timeout 5, batch_size 1, flush_batch_tick_timeout 100. Ordinary appends are paced at 4ms so consecutive decided-index changes are observed in separate ticks; a burst would decide many entries inside one tick gap and emit a single amalgamated event. Case unconsumed_event_stream_stops_actor_loop leaves each node's event receiver unread (the handle owns one from spawn_actor even if the application never calls subscribe_events) and emits CA_EVENT unconsumed_event_bound_reached {nodes_full,nodes,event_capacity}, CA_EVENT actor_parked {node,samples_without_reply,reply_budget_ms,permanently_parked} and CA_EVENT append_notify_endpoint_withheld {node,per_call_deadline_ms,actor_timeout_ms,outer_wait_ms,resolved}. Case drained_event_stream_keeps_actor_loop_running is the control with one difference, a task per node draining the same stream, and emits CA_EVENT control_actors_responsive {nodes_answering,nodes,event_capacity} and CA_EVENT control_append_notify {origin,succeeded,idx}.

prefix.before: Three real OmniPaxos instances (pid 1,2,3) are built with OmniPaxosConfig::build over omnipaxos_storage::memory_storage::MemoryStorage and driven by three real omnipaxos_runtime actors spawned with spawn_actor, using a harness-local `TestRuntime` (tokio-backed AsyncRuntime impl; the crate's TokioRuntime behind the tokio_runtime feature is not required). An in-process transport task per node forwards every message from that node's `outgoing_messages()` to the receiver returned by `msg.get_receiver()`. RuntimeConfig: tick_period 2ms, egress_period 1ms, event_capacity 64, append_notify_timeout 1500ms; ServerConfig: election_tick_timeout 3, resend_message_tick_timeout 5, batch_size 1, flush_batch_tick_timeout 100. Proposals are paced at 4ms so consecutive decided-index changes are observed in separate ticks (a burst would decide many entries inside one tick gap and produce a single amalgamated event). Case `unconsumed_event_stream_stops_actor_loop` leaves each node's event receiver unread (the handle always owns one after spawn_actor; the application never calls subscribe_events or never reads it) while ordinary appends keep the cluster busy until all three event channels are full; case `drained_event_stream_keeps_actor_loop_running` is the same cluster, capacity and activity with one difference: a task per node drains the event stream. The decisive evidence of case 1 is (a) all three event channels full with a live (not closed) receiver, (b) at least one node whose actor never answers a `decided_idx` command again across ten 200ms samples, (c) that parked node's `append_notify_with_timeout(.., 300ms)` not resolving inside 4s although the actor that would produce its Timeout runs on that same tick path; the assertion messages print the observed channel state. Case 2 requires every node to keep answering and a fresh append_notify from a follower to resolve Ok(idx>=1).

experiments.revision_reason: Same probe, cluster/configuration and the same two cases, but the harness now prints CA_EVENT JSON lines with the observed operands (bound reached, parked node, withheld endpoint, control responsiveness, control append_notify) so the receipt carries parsed observations a conclusion can cite; the previous receipt ran both cases green but recorded no parsed events.

interpretations.rationale: Current account (source-only, no receipt yet): the blocking behavior itself is settled by source - detect_and_emit_events publishes every observed transition with `event_tx.send(..).await` (omnipaxos_runtime/src/actor.rs:169-199) and is awaited in the tick arm of the only actor loop (actor.rs:665-711); the event channel is bounded (RuntimeConfig::event_capacity, handle.rs:34-35, default 1024 at handle.rs:74) and subscribe_events hands out a shared receiver clone (handle.rs:254-259). With a live-but-unread receiver the send is Pending and the actor task parks, so op.tick() (which drives leader-election heartbeats, message resends and batch flushes), handle_incoming and command handling all stop; a caller then cannot even obtain the documented append_notify failure endpoint, because the Timeout is produced by drain_notifiers on that same tick path (actor.rs:201-222, contract at handle.rs:114-137). Sibling paths of the same actor were built to avoid exactly this (try_send + buffering in drain_outgoing_buf, actor.rs:232-258; try_send + defer in push_to_all_subs, actor.rs:301-333), and the crate's own regression test asserts the invariant for the outgoing channel ('must still be responsive... if flush_outgoing blocked on a full channel, this would hang', tests/async_runtime_test.rs:1040-1082). What is NOT yet established: an actual execution showing the parked loop and its consequence. A first local construction of the probe (draft/assurance_generated.rs: 3-node in-process cluster, event_capacity=1, subscribe_events() receiver retained and never read) compiled and ran, but the harness as written did not reach the expected state - no node blocked within 500ms, and even the drained-events control cluster had not decided an entry within the probe's 300ms append_notify deadline, so the cluster had presumably not yet progressed to a second observed transition/two-state leader view. Until the probe is repaired and executed through the controller, the freeze and its consequence stay unverified. Counter-limitations to carry: (a) the trigger is client-side usage (a retained but unread receiver) - the runtime documents no drain obligation, and event_capacity only delays the parking, it does not bound it; (b) a receiver that is dropped unblocks the actor (the send error is ignored), so the stall lasts exactly as long as the receiver is held; (c) no source in the snapshot states that the actor loop must stay responsive to a full event channel, so the finding rests on the contract of the handle methods (every Command-reply method, including append_notify's Timeout) plus the deliberate non-blocking design of the sibling egress paths.

Current account. Settled by source: every transition the actor observes is published with an awaited send on a channel created once in spawn_actor as async_channel::bounded(RuntimeConfig::event_capacity) (handle.rs:295-323, capacity field handle.rs:34-35, default 1024 at handle.rs:74); detect_and_emit_events issues those sends (actor.rs:169-199) and is awaited from inside the tick arm of the single run select loop (actor.rs:665-711), so a Pending send there stops op.tick(), incoming handling, command handling and decided-subscriber pushes. subscribe_events hands out a clone of that same receiver (handle.rs:254-259), and append_notify's Timeout endpoint is produced by drain_notifiers on the same tick path (actor.rs:201-222, contract handle.rs:114-137), so a parked actor would also withhold that documented failure. NOT settled: whether an unread receiver actually parks the actor. Local construction (native feedback, not retained receipts; harness draft/assurance_generated.rs) produced two contradicting observations on the same cluster shape (3 nodes, in-process transport, event_capacity=1, tick_period=2ms): (A) with no consumer task at all, i.e. only the receiver the handle itself holds, no node reached a stable leader within 10s and every current_leader() poll timed out - consistent with the park; (B) with a per-node consumer task that reads events during a healthy phase (leader elected, entries decided, all commands answered) and then stops reading while keeping the receiver (instrumented: the task confirmed it had stopped reading), the cluster went on deciding all 24 further proposals and every node kept answering commands, and a later append_notify succeeded - inconsistent with the park. Because both variants leave an unread receiver on a bounded channel, (B) defeats the currently stated premise that 'unread receiver + capacity reached => sender stays Pending'. Possible explanations not yet distinguished: the tick arm's send may not be the blocking point in (B) (e.g. produces no further events, or the send resolves immediately because the channel is closed/space exists), or (A)'s no-progress has a different cause than the one claimed. Until the decisive channel-state observation is made, the freeze and its consequence stay unverified, so no defect is asserted. Counter-limitations to carry: a dropped receiver would unblock the actor (the send error is ignored), capacity only delays the parking, no snapshot source states that the actor loop must stay responsive to a full event channel (the finding would rest on the handle-method contract plus the deliberate try_send design of the sibling egress paths), and the event_capacity=1 configuration is an extreme point of a knob whose default is 1024.
limitations: Local construction observations (harness drafts run by the agent, not controller receipts) cannot support a formal conclusion; variant (B) also used an agent-defined tokio-backed AsyncRuntime implementation rather than the crate's TokioRuntime feature.
The parked-actor consequence for the rest of the cluster (lost quorum participation) has not been observed at all, only the node-local command/append_notify endpoints.

interpretations.rationale: Current account. Source-settled: the actor publishes each observed transition with `event_tx.send(..).await` inside `detect_and_emit_events` (actor.rs:169-199), awaited from the tick arm of the single `run` select loop (actor.rs:665-711), on the channel spawn_actor creates as async_channel::bounded(RuntimeConfig::event_capacity) (handle.rs:295-323; capacity knob handle.rs:34-35, default 1024 handle.rs:74). The handle owns a receiver from construction, so an application that ignores the event stream still leaves it unread; a Pending send there stops op.tick() (election heartbeat, resends, batch flush), incoming handling, command handling and decided-subscriber pushes, and also withholds append_notify's Timeout, which drain_notifiers would emit on the same tick path (actor.rs:201-222, contract handle.rs:114-137). Previous contradiction resolved during construction (local feedback, not receipts): the stalled-consumer variant had not frozen because the burst of proposals was decided inside a single tick gap, so only one further transition was observed and the channel never took a second send; instrumented runs showed the channel at len=1/capacity=1 with a parked actor in the no-consumer variant, and len=0 with a running actor in the burst variant. The probe is now paced (one proposal per 4ms) and reaches the bound on all three nodes at event_capacity=64, where the local runs (two consecutive, unmodified sources) show: all three channels full with live receivers, at least one actor loop parked and never answering again, its append_notify_with_timeout(300ms) unresolved after 4s, while the drained-stream control keeps all nodes answering and resolves a follower append_notify Ok(idx>=1). Defect judgment stays unresolved until the retained execution reports those comparisons; the claim under test is scoped to: a node whose client does not consume its event stream parks its actor loop once event_capacity transitions are observed, permanently losing ticks and every command reply (including the documented failure endpoints), and its participation is lost to the cluster. Counter-limitations carried forward: the trigger is client-side usage with no documented drain obligation, event_capacity only delays the parking, a dropped receiver unblocks the actor (send error ignored), no snapshot source states that a full event channel must not park the loop, and the cluster-level consequence at the default capacity (1024) is not observed by this probe.
limitations: The probe reaches the bound at event_capacity=64; it does not witness the same freeze at the default 1024, and it does not measure how many unconsumed transitions a real deployment would need.

Only the node-local consequences are asserted (command round-tripping and the append_notify endpoint); no quorum-level consequence is measured, and the parked-set is reported as `at least one node`, not as all nodes.
Local construction runs used a harness-local tokio-backed AsyncRuntime impl rather than the crate's TokioRuntime feature; the formal receipt will use the controller's clean copy.

interpretations.rationale: Current account. Source-settled mechanism: the actor publishes every observed transition with `event_tx.send(..).await` inside `detect_and_emit_events` (actor.rs:169-199), awaited from the tick arm of the single `run` select loop (actor.rs:665-711), on the channel spawn_actor builds as `async_channel::bounded(RuntimeConfig::event_capacity)` (handle.rs:295-323; knob handle.rs:34-35, default 1024 handle.rs:74). The handle owns a receiver from construction, so an application that never consumes the event stream still leaves it unread, and `subscribe_events` only hands out clones of that same channel (handle.rs:254-259). A `send` that cannot fit parks the actor task, which then cannot run `op.tick()` (election heartbeats, resends, batch flushes), cannot handle incoming messages, and cannot answer any Command - including the `append_notify` Timeout that `drain_notifiers` would have produced on that same tick path (actor.rs:201-222; endpoint documented at handle.rs:114-137). The crate's sibling egress paths avoid exactly this with `try_send` (drain_outgoing_buf; push_to_sub/push_to_all_subs) and its own regression test states the invariant for the outgoing channel. Recorded execution 011decb17a314e839b860436ad3dc164 (experiment 9a11299aa4344bb5b84565cbe33701ad-experiment, exit 0) ran the two-case harness against the clean copy and its test_selection reports both cases passed: `unconsumed_event_stream_stops_actor_loop` and `drained_event_stream_keeps_actor_loop_running` (nothing filtered out). Case 1 (event_capacity 64, paced 4ms proposals, no consumer) required and observed: all three event channels full (`len == capacity`, receiver not closed), at least one node whose actor never answered a `decided_idx` command across ten 200ms samples and still answered nothing 500ms later, and that node's `append_notify_with_timeout(.., 300ms)` unresolved after 4s although its `append_notify_timeout` is 1500ms. Case 2 (identical cluster, capacity and activity, with a task draining each event stream) required and observed the opposite: every node kept answering commands and a follower `append_notify` resolved `Ok(idx >= 1)`. Because the only difference between the cases is whether the event stream is consumed, the parking and the withheld endpoints are attributed to the unconsumed bounded event channel, not to the transport, the configuration or the harness. Scope of the defect asserted: a node whose client does not consume its event stream permanently stops participating (no ticks, no message handling, no command replies) once it has observed `event_capacity` transitions, for any finite capacity - the probe reaches that bound at 64 to stay inside a bounded window, and the source-settled mechanism is capacity-independent. Counter-limitations, kept in force: (a) the trigger is client-side usage and no snapshot source states a drain obligation, so the defect rests on the handle-method contract (every Command reply, and the documented Timeout) plus the deliberate non-blocking design of the sibling egress paths; (b) a receiver that is dropped unblocks the actor (the send error is ignored), so the stall lasts exactly as long as a live receiver exists; (c) the receipt witnesses the bound at 64 with node-local endpoints only - no observation at the 1024 default and no quorum-level measurement of the other nodes losing this participant; (d) the receipt has no parsed events (the harness asserts rather than emitting event lines), so its decisive content is the two recorded test outcomes, not parsed indices. That receipt recorded no parsed observations (event_count 0), so it cannot be cited as completed support and this account stays conditional: the defect is asserted on the source plus that recorded run, and a revised harness emitting CA_EVENT operands was submitted for a fresh execution so a later account can cite parsed indices.
limitations: Capacity-independence and practical reachability at the default 1024 are argued from source, not observed: the execution reached the bound at event_capacity=64.

Only node-local endpoints are witnessed (command round-trips and the append_notify endpoint); the consequence for the rest of the cluster (lost quorum participant, leadership churn caused by the silent node) is not measured.
The receipt carries no parsed events (event_count 0), so no zero-based indices are available for it; the decisive record is the receipt's test outcomes.

The stalled-consumer variant from earlier construction is superseded as evidence: its non-freeze was traced to proposals being decided inside a single tick gap, which coalesced transitions; the retained probe paces proposals instead.

interpretations.rationale: Source-only current account of the new question, no execution yet. A follower replies to each AcceptDecide/AcceptStopSign with an Accepted that carries only the receipt's ballot and the follower's accepted_idx (follower.rs:160-175), and the leader turns those receipts into a decision when `is_chosen` sees a quorum of advertised accepted indexes (leader.rs:316-345). Both roles have a periodic callback - SequencePaxos::resend_message_timeout dispatches to resend_messages_leader/resend_messages_follower every resend_message_tick_timeout logical ticks (mod.rs:229-246) - but in the accept phase the leader's version only resends a pending StopSign (or its decide) and re-Prepares peers that are not promised (leader.rs:371-403), and the follower's version is the empty `Phase::Accept => ()` arm (follower.rs:240-269); the follower's other periodic path, flush_batch_follower, replies only when the batch flush itself advanced the accepted index (follower.rs:284-290). So the direction follower->leader has no timer-driven retry, and the leader has no way to ask a follower for its accepted index; the only later trigger is a new AcceptDecide arriving for new entries, which makes the follower advertise a (possibly larger) accepted_idx. Whether that leaves a genuinely quorum-accepted entry undecided for an unbounded interval with no enabled repair under normal (no further proposal) conditions is exactly what the registered discriminator is to decide; no defect is claimed before it runs.
limitations: The claim depends on the environment being permitted to lose a single message while the transport keeps the rest in order; the probe must drop only the Accepted reply and keep delivering everything else.

A retry of the client's own proposal (in the runtime layer) can repair the earlier entry as a side effect, so any later assertion must be scoped to 'no further proposal is made', which the core API does not itself require of a caller.
